C-FUNCTIONAL-VOCABULARY.Summary: Reconcile the English and Russian governing vocabulary around functional interpretation, responsibilities, boundaries and equivalent meaning.

Goals.Goal: Review all defined terms, states and stage groups in both editions against each other and the governing clauses.
Replace ambiguous related-word lists with explicit interpretive distinctions and correct omissions or narrowed meanings without changing the operating model.
Maintain the shared terminology reference as one accepted set without gray or white classifications, distinct from the governing vocabulary's interpretive purpose.

Constraints.Constraint: Authority: the user requested a clean, meaningful charter vocabulary in both language folders, focused on functional interpretation with no drift. Reuse this authorization for the bounded reconciliation and its portal projection.

Preserve existing authorities, commitments, decision rights, risk controls, measurement populations, state transitions, record identities, document precedence and language neutrality. Corrections are grounded in current governing clauses.
Preserve unrelated working-tree changes and previous approved GRACE bundles. No unsupported claim of measured international acceptance.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Rewriting the entire corpus's naming, adding governance policy, changing legal obligations, translating proper names, apply/archive, commit, push or deployment.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Both governing vocabulary editions state their interpretive function and relationship to the shared naming reference in formal language.
All definitions, state meanings and stage descriptions are semantically paired; distinctions describe relationships, not bare alternate-word lists.
Acceptance authority, delegation, record classes and common business concepts agree with the existing governing clauses.
Source metadata, relevant current descriptions and generated portal pages agree with the reconciled edition; checks and browser verification pass.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Paired semantic review with governing sources and browser checks of both vocabulary pages.
